hook_spec.mechanism: TranspositionTable::reseed(new_salt) (src/search/tt/table.rs): set the salt, drain every valid entry in native bucket order, clear, re-place each through the normal insertion path (insert_new) under the new index function; overflow resolved by the incumbent eviction policy; generation fields preserved; never invents values, never writes to a key's wrong bucket. Call site: Search::reseed_at_boundary, invoked from bounded_search exactly where the chunk loop continues (after a full-work chunk, before growth); natural-exhaustion/decisive/resource-cut exits and the final partial chunk never reseed. Salt sequence s_{k+1} = s_k + 1 (wrapping), deterministic in the starting salt. History/killers and the repetition cache untouched.
hook_spec.memory_note: the spike stages the drained entries in a transient Vec (~100 MB at 128 MB table / ~95% occupancy); a productized reseed should rehash in bounded extra space
hook_spec.no_layout_change: two entries per bucket unchanged; no new entry fields; snapshot contract untouched

d3_k1_retention.note: retention = after/before per reseed side-band line; live/solved/unsolved counted as in TT::stats() (all entries are current-generation during a search run: new_generation is never called by the search)
d3_k1_retention.K1_verdict: FIRED on every stress-class retention run: live retention 79.4-83.8% (< 85%) at the >= ~80%-occupancy reseeds on stress s0 rs1 (k=8,9), stress s1 rs1 (k=8,9), and stress s0 rsg (k=2,3); solved retention stays >= 97.6% everywhere (the incumbent policy protects solved entries). Per plan20 Gates: PIVOT - the 'TT-keeping' premise is materially violated at the occupancies where the lever is supposed to act; #20 closes at Phase 0 with this table as the no-go record.
d3_k1_retention.mechanism_note: the loss is structural, not an implementation artifact: re-placing N entries into 2-slot buckets under a fresh index loses every arrival that hits a full bucket (the incumbent eviction policy drops the victim, exactly as a normal store does). At occupancy alpha the per-bucket arrival count is ~Poisson(2*alpha); E[min(arrivals,2)]/live at alpha=0.947 is ~74.7% under a uniform index - the observed 79.4% is slightly better (imperfectly uniform index + the work/solved priority), i.e. the measured loss is at the physics of capacity-2 rehashing, not at the edge of implementable behavior for the pinned mechanism.
